IRS990.MissionDesc: THE BRANDEIS SCHOOL OF SAN FRANCISCO INSPIRES STUDENTS TO LEAD LIVES OF LEARNING AND PURPOSE. WE PROVIDE A CHALLENGING ACADEMIC ENVIRONMENT AND A WELCOMING, INCLUSIVE COMMUNITY, EACH DEEPLY ENRICHED BY JEWISH THOUGHT, VALUES, AND TRADITIONS.
IRS990.Desc: AT THE BRANDEIS SCHOOL OF SAN FRANCISCO, WE BELIEVE THAT TRUE LEARNING HAPPENS ONLY WHEN KNOWLEDGE IS CONNECTED TO PURPOSE. WE KNOW THAT WHAT OUR STUDENTS LEARN AT BRANDEIS TODAY WILL MATTER TO THE WORLD TOMORROW, AND WE STRIVE TO EDUCATE PEOPLE CAPABLE OF MAKING MEANINGFUL CONTRIBUTIONS. OUR CHALLENGING K-8 ACADEMIC ENVIRONMENT IS FOCUSED ON RELEVANCE AND ROOTED IN JEWISH VALUES, TRADITIONS, AND CULTURE.

BusinessName.BusinessNameLine1Txt: MALIKA DENSBY DIRECTOR OF FINANCE AND OPERATIONS

SupplementalInformationDetail.ExplanationTxt: ENDOWMENT FUNDS HELD BY THE SCHOOL ARE INVESTED TO PROVIDE A STABLE LONG-TERM FUNDING SOURCE FOR NEED-BASED STUDENT SCHOLARSHIPS AND SUPPORT OTHER OPERATIONAL NEEDS OF THE SCHOOL.

THE SCHOOL IS A QUALIFIED NOT-FOR-PROFIT ORGANIZATION EXEMPT FROM FEDERAL INCOME AND CALIFORNIA FRANCHISE TAXES UNDER THE PROVISIONS OF SECTIONS 501(C)(3) OF THE INTERNAL REVENUE CODE AND 23701(D) OF THE CALIFORNIA REVENUE AND TAXATION CODE, RESPECTIVELY. THE SCHOOL HAS EVALUATED ITS CURRENT TAX POSITIONS AND HAS CONCLUDED THAT AS OF JUNE 30, 2025, THE SCHOOL DOES NOT HAVE ANY SIGNIFICANT UNCERTAIN TAX POSITIONS FOR WHICH A RESERVE WOULD BE NECESSARY.
FINANCIAL AID 4,846,282. AUXILIARY/TRANSPORTATION EXPENSES 293,729. PARENT ASSOCIATION FEES 35,100.
THE SCHOOL PUBLISHES ITS RACIALLY NONDISCRIMINATORY POLICY ON THE HOMEPAGE OF ITS WEBSITE AT ALL OF THE TIME DURING THE YEAR IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE REQUIREMENTS INCLUDED IN REVENUE RULING 2019-22.

PER SCHOOL POLICY, FINANCIAL AID IS PROVIDED TO STUDENTS BASED ON FINANCIAL NEED. APPLICANTS FOR ENROLLMENT IN THE SCHOOL ARE EVALUATED ON A BLIND BASIS WITHOUT REGARD TO ABILITY TO PAY. AMOUNT OF AID AWARDED EACH YEAR IS USUALLY LIMITED TO THE AMOUNT OF AID BUDGETED BY THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS.

THE BOARD APPROVED THE EMPLOYMENT AGREEMENT INCLUDING COMPENSATION PACKAGE FOR HEAD OF SCHOOL. THE HEAD OF SCHOOL(HOS) RECEIVED A HOUSING ALLOWANCE OF $40,000 IN 2024, WHICH WAS INCLUDED ON SCHEDULE J, PART II, COLUMN (B).
THE BOARD APPROVED THE EMPLOYMENT AGREEMENT INCLUDING COMPENSATION PACKAGE FOR HEAD OF SCHOOL.

SupplementalInformationDetail.FormAndLineReferenceDesc: FORM 990, PART VI, SECTION B, LINE 11B
SupplementalInformationDetail.ExplanationTxt: THE ORGANIZATION PROVIDED A COMPLETE COPY OF FORM 990 TO ITS GOVERNING BODY FOR REVIEW BEFORE FILING.

SupplementalInformationDetail.FormAndLineReferenceDesc: FORM 990, PART VI, SECTION B, LINE 12C
SupplementalInformationDetail.ExplanationTxt: THE SCHOOL REQUIRES ALL OFFICERS, BOARD MEMBERS AND KEY EMPLOYEES ANNUALLY SIGN A CONFLICT OF INTEREST POLICY. THESE ARE REVIEWED BY THE PRESIDENT OF THE BOARD OF TRUSTEES AND THE HEAD OF SCHOOL. THOSE WITH A CONFLICT OF INTEREST ARE ASKED TO RECUSE THEMSELVES FROM ANY DECISIONS THAT WOULD BE AFFECTED BY THE EXISTENCE OF SAID CONFLICT.

SupplementalInformationDetail.FormAndLineReferenceDesc: FORM 990, PART VI, SECTION B, LINE 15
SupplementalInformationDetail.ExplanationTxt: THE SCHOOL PARTICIPATES IN LOCAL AND NATIONAL SURVEYS WHICH COLLECTS INFORMATION ABOUT COMPENSATION FOR MANAGEMENT AND KEY EMPLOYEES.

SupplementalInformationDetail.FormAndLineReferenceDesc: FORM 990, PART VI, SECTION C, LINE 19
SupplementalInformationDetail.ExplanationTxt: THE ORGANIZATION MAKES AVAILABLE ITS GOVERNING DOCUMENTS, CONFLICT OF INTEREST POLICY, AND AUDITED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS UPON REQUEST FOR THE SAME PERIOD OF TIME SET FORTH IN SEC. 6104(D).
